questions.question_text:
A solution has hydrogen-ion concentration $M=10^{-8}$ mol/L.
Using $pH=-\log_{10}M$, what is its pH?

options.why: Multiplied the calculated pH of $8$ by ten, incorrectly using the decibel factor.
Forgot the minus sign in $pH=-\log_{10}M$.
Gave the concentration $10^{-8}$ as a number instead of its pH.

questions.question_text:
One earthquake has Richter magnitude $7$ and another has magnitude $5$.
Using $A=10^{M}$, how many times greater is the amplitude of the magnitude-$7$ earthquake?

options.why: Used the magnitude difference $7-5=2$ directly instead of evaluating $10^{2}$.
Calculated $10^{7}$ for the larger amplitude without dividing by $10^{5}$.
Divided the magnitudes, calculating $7/5$, instead of dividing the amplitudes.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{A_{1}}{A_{2}}=\dfrac{10^{7}}{10^{5}}$
$=10^{2}$
$=100$
So the amplitude is $100$ times greater.

questions.question_text:
One earthquake measures magnitude $6$ and another measures magnitude $2$ on the Richter scale.
How many times greater is the amplitude of the larger earthquake?

options.why: Used the difference in magnitude directly instead of $10^{4}$.
Raised ten to the larger magnitude instead of the difference.
Divided the magnitudes rather than subtracting them.
Used the difference of $2$ magnitudes instead of $10^{2}$.
Treated the two-step gap as a single times-ten step.
Used a difference of three magnitudes instead of two.

questions.solution_text:
From the graph, Tonga has magnitude $6$ and Alaska has magnitude $4$.
$\dfrac{A_{1}}{A_{2}}=\dfrac{10^{6}}{10^{4}}$
$=10^{2}$
$=100$
So the amplitude was $100$ times greater.

questions.question_text:
How many times more intense is a $90$ dB sound than a $40$ dB sound?
Use $\dfrac{I}{I_{0}}=10^{S/10}$.

options.why: Used the decibel difference of $50$ directly as the answer.
Stopped at the index $5$ instead of evaluating $10^{5}$.
Used a difference of $30$ dB instead of $50$ dB.

questions.question_text:
On a base-$10$ logarithmic scale, the volume of Lake P has magnitude $7$ and the volume of Lake Q has magnitude $3$.
Lake Q holds $2000$ ML of water.
How much water does Lake P hold?

options.why: Multiplied $2000$ by the magnitude difference $4$ instead of by $10^{4}$.
Used $7\times10^{3}$ as the multiplier instead of $10^{7-3}$.
Used a magnitude difference of $2$ instead of $4$, multiplying $2000$ by $10^{2}$.

questions.solution_text:
The magnitudes differ by $7-3=4$.
So Lake P holds $10^{4}=10\,000$ times as much water.
$2000\times10\,000=20\,000\,000$ ML

questions.question_text:
A solution has $pH=2.5$.
Using $pH=-\log_{10}M$, what is its hydrogen-ion concentration in mol/L?
Give your answer to $3$ significant figures.

options.why: Used $10^{-1.5}$ instead of $10^{-2.5}$, making the concentration ten times too large.
Forgot the negative sign in the exponent and evaluated $10^{2.5}$ to $3$ significant figures.
Stopped at $\log_{10}M=-2.5$ and gave the logarithm as the concentration.

questions.solution_text:
$pH=-\log_{10}M$
$\log_{10}M=-pH$
$M=10^{-pH}$
$=10^{-2.5}$
$\approx0.0031622777$
So the concentration is $0.00316$ mol/L to $3$ significant figures.
